body:
The twenty-eighth of September begins at a border. It has a cathedral, a death list and no new clause.

I. The city that changed hands

Leo XIV flies at morning from Lourdes to Metz. Touchdown at twenty past nine at Metz-Nancy-Lorraine. The city has been German and French by turns. It counts three borders and a cathedral of stone and glass. 1

At ten he meets the faiths in the Robert Schuman congress hall. Catholics, Protestants, Jews, Muslims, Orthodox, Buddhists. A joint paper is on the sheet. Paper is not a front. 1

At eleven he speaks of roots, peace and unity. Emmanuel Macron sits with him. Other European heads are invited. Strasbourg is left aside. The guest chooses the source, not the parliament. 2

Robert Schuman lies six kilometres on, in Scy-Chazelles. The house with the narrow bed and the blue inkwell is not on the plan. The pope will not see the desk where, in 1950, a sentence on coal and steel was written. He speaks in the building that bears the name. The grave stays unvisited. 3

Afternoon: the popemobile from Avenue Foch to Saint-Étienne Cathedral. Two kilometres of streets. Belgians, Luxembourgers, Germans are expected. Sixty thousand in the city. Twelve thousand at the cathedral and the yard beyond. 4

Mass at four. The cathedral altar holds bronze from old German guns. The metal that once fired now holds cup and book. Farewell at the airport at half past six. Wheels up at seven for Rome. Fiumicino near nine. 3 4

The journey was named “That a world may have life.” Four days in France. Paris, Lourdes, Metz. The white guest’s thread ends on Monday night. It closes because the journey is over. The finger does not stay at the grotto. It stays on the tap and on the field.

A border that changed masters three times hears a speech on unity. The field in the east hears drones.

II. The list that keeps running

Across Sunday eight people die in Ukraine. One woman in Russia. The tallies differ. The direction does not. Sumy, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa, Kyiv and the capital’s rim. 5

In Sumy, glide bombs hit a family centre. Three dead, among them a sixteen-year-old girl. Five wounded. The interior minister gives the number on Sunday. The city sits on the border Moscow wants as a buffer. 7

In Zaporizhzhia region three die in the night. Houses, a car. In the morning another blow on a house in the city. The field needs no fresh metaphor. It has street names. 5

West of Kyiv, in Sofiiska Borshchahivka, a drone hits a market. Two dead, about ten hurt. Stalls burn. Vehicles sit crooked. The pictures still move on Monday morning because smoke does not keep office hours. 6

In Kyiv itself a man dies to a drone. Klitschko counts the wounded, among them teenagers. A nine-storey block in Darnytskyi. Schools and kindergartens scarred. A data centre struck twice at morning. Three hurt in the first blow, two of them children. Kyivstar reports damage at its headquarters. Moscow names Vodafone. The lines are the target, not only the battery. 5 6

Odesa calls it a mass strike. One dead. A home, a shop, a hotel, a clinic, a grain store. Two cargo ships bound for the port, Russia’s defence ministry says. The Black Sea keeps the same ledger. 5

Zelenskyy puts the week on the table again. More than two thousand two hundred attack drones. About one thousand six hundred bombs from the air. Thirty-eight missiles. He says a power that meant to ease off would not send this wave. The sentence sits on the wire. The field answers with sirens. 5

In Enerhodar, under Russian administration, a civilian woman dies in a Ukrainian strike, the installed mayor says. Belgorod counts one dead on the other side. The book takes both numbers. The field has no margin for a footnote.

Monday changes no file in Miami. It changes the list.

III. The tap that stays shut

Tehran does not yield. On Sunday Araghchi says the seven days still stand. Mediators: Qatar, Oman, Pakistan. A second sitting after the UN week has no date. Washington refused the plan. No one lays a new clause. 8

Ship-counters say the blockade remains on. Blasts near Qeshm were reported. They grew no treaty. Tehran shows a second undersea craft it says it seized. Washington still says it already holds the water. 8

Trump stays in Tennessee. Willing to talk. Lawn terms unchanged. The tap has received no new word. It stands where it stood.

Oil looks for detours. Fees, dark transits, temporary lanes. The needle stays a needle. Whoever means to turn the tap needs more than a refusal and more than an offer.

IV. At the edge of the page

In Kohat, Pakistan, an attack hits a police compound. At least thirty-one dead. The book counts the yard because the great halls do not. 9

Two pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, reach Atlanta. Last week’s gift lands at the zoo. The trade council promised them. The bears keep the date. The clauses on Taiwan do not. 9

Aleksandar Vučić resigns in order to run for prime minister. Ana Brnabić holds the office for now. Switzerland rejects an initiative that would have written a harder neutrality into the constitution and barred sanctions and NATO work. France has chosen its Senate by indirect vote. São Tomé has chosen an assembly. 9

In Berlin Guye Adola and Tigst Assefa cross the line. Assefa cramps before the tape and still wins. In Shenzhen the Czechs take the Billie Jean King Cup from Ukraine, two–nil. The field sends no side to the sand. 9

On Tuesday Washington means to bar Canadian goods: motorcycles, certain whey, molasses, beer. Ottawa has already counted the list. Customs writes more sharply than some treaties. 10

Ethiopia: a drone hits Tigrai Television in Mekelle. The station goes dark. TPLF takes Erebti in Afar. Afghanistan says it killed twenty-eight fighters it ties to Islamic State and seized thirty-two more. Mekelle and Kohat are not on the Europe speech. They sit on the edge. 9

Kyiv spent fifteen hours under alert on Sunday. Jet-powered drones fly higher. The defences catch fewer. Zelenskyy names two kindergartens and two schools in the capital alone. A garage burns. Warehouses burn. Who hits housing hits winter early.

Last week’s licence builds no battery today. Putin remains invited to Miami. Brussels remains set to condemn. No line on the ground moves because a name is spoken in Metz.

The border at Metz is a bridge today. It was a ditch. The chronicler counts both, because one does not erase the other. Schuman wrote of concrete steps. Monday delivers a speech and a mass. The field delivers addresses.

Ethiopia: a drone hits Tigrai Television in Mekelle. The station goes dark. TPLF takes Erebti in Afar and pushes toward Afdera. Afghanistan says it killed twenty-eight fighters it ties to Islamic State and seized thirty-two. In The Hague Hashim Thaçi is sentenced to twenty-five years. The verdict sits far from Metz. It still belongs on the page.

In Northern Ireland the Orange Order may march again through a Catholic quarter, by court order, for the first time in thirty years. The road is blocked. The parade runs late. Old routes need new stamps.

Thailand’s constitutional court is due on Monday to rule on the February election. A sentence may void part of the result. The book notes the date, not the ruling that has not yet come.

Munich bids for the Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044. The German committee has chosen the city. The train to Metz is shorter than the wait for the Games.

Whoever sees only the congress hall sees flags. Whoever reads the margin sees a market outside Kyiv and a police yard in Kohat. The book keeps both sides on one sheet.

On Tuesday customs means to bar motorcycles and molasses. On Monday no one turns the tap. That is the order of the page.

The chronicler’s close

The white guest has the border behind him. The journey is over. The field has new names in Sumy, outside Kyiv and on the Black Sea. The tap has received no clause.

Open remain Hormuz without a treaty and the eastern field. The two thrones rest. The hall of nations rests. The guest is closed because he lands in Rome.

The World Book does not close. It leaves a finger in the pages and waits for 29 September.
